title: Model catalog prioritization & benchmark walkthrough - Solaris Finance
next_steps: Maya to share shortlist + cost/latency spreadsheet by 2026-04-02
Liam to provision a short bench run for Solaris test prompts (2-3 models) - target week of 2026-04-05
Sophia to confirm compliance stakeholders and preferred data residency by 2026-04-06
action_items: Maya Patel: Send model shortlist + pricing & tier options (due 2026-04-02)
Liam Chen: Run 1k-token latency/throughput bench on g4dn and a8g for 3 candidate models (due 2026-04-09)
Sophia Kim: Share SOC2 scope and any additional audit questions (due 2026-04-06)
Daniel Ruiz: Provide 10 representative prompts and a success criteria doc (due 2026-04-03)
summary: Redwood ran a focused walkthrough of the model catalog, prioritization heuristics, and benching options for Solaris Finance. Primary concerns: latency targets for synchronous APIs (<=200ms P95 for short queries), cost per 1k tokens, VPC/private deployment constraints, and audit logs/KMS. Agreed next steps: shortlist + bench run, share security package, schedule follow-up pilot planning.
topics: Bench setup and metrics (latency, throughput, tokens/sec)
Compatibility matrix (quantization, kernel mapping, hardware fit)
transcript: 00:00:00 - Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
00:00:05 - Olivia Park: Olivia here, CTO at Solaris. Hi Maya, Liam, nice to meet Aria as well.
00:00:10 - Daniel Ruiz: Daniel, ML eng — I'll be the technical owner for the bench runs.
00:00:13 - Sophia Kim: Sophia, platform lead. we'll be looking at VPC/on-prem options.

00:00:20 - Maya Patel: Awesome. agenda — we'll do a short demo of the catalog UI, then show how we prioritize models with the compatibility matrix, and end with how Optimize suggests batching/quantization. leave time for Q&A at the end.
00:00:35 - Liam Chen: quick note — I'll jump into the runtime implications when we look at kernel mapping and hardware fit.
00:00:42 - Ethan Brooks: Ethan, product — mainly listening, may ask about model quality tradeoffs.

00:00:50 - Maya Patel: Great. starting in the console — catalog view. so you can filter by task, sequence length distribution, and inference cost. um, Olivia — you mentioned most calls are short customer queries, 40-80 tokens typically?
00:01:05 - Olivia Park: Yeah that's right, 80 tokens max usually. but we also have some doc-summary flows that go longer, so we care about mixed workloads.

00:01:12 - Maya Patel: Perfect. so first filter — latency-first. when you pick latency-first, the catalog shows models that our runtime has profiled with low tail latency on the selected hardware families. you can also toggle 'cost-aware' and 'quality-prioritized'.
00:01:28 - Daniel Ruiz: how granular is the latency profiling? like p50/p95 across token lengths?
00:01:33 - Aria Soto: yes, we break down by p50/p95/p99, and by sequence length buckets (<=64, 65-512, 512+). the console shows sample runs and the underlying benchmark CSV you can download.
00:01:45 - Sophia Kim: is the data from your hosted infra or from dedicated runs? we need numbers that match the Dedicated footprints if we go that route.

00:01:52 - Liam Chen: good question. the catalog shows both: verified hosted profiles and dedicated/reserved profiles. for dedicated we re-run the bench on the same kernel/quantization settings you'd pick, so it's aligned with the Dedicated SKU.
00:02:05 - Ethan Brooks: do you show estimated cost per 1k tokens?

00:02:08 - Maya Patel: yes, estimated unit economics — it factors in batching heuristics and typical KV cache hit rates. it's an estimate — for hard numbers we'd run a targeted bench with your payloads.
00:02:20 - Olivia Park: talk to me about compatibility matrix — I want to understand which models work with int8 quantization and which break because of custom ops.

00:02:27 - Aria Soto: the compatibility matrix maps model families to kernel support, quantization health, and known fallbacks. for example, some newer LLM variants need custom attention kernels and show reduced perf when naively quantized. we annotate that and suggest model variants that are quantization-friendly.
00:02:41 - Daniel Ruiz: does that include 4-bit/LLM.int8 style profiles? we've been experimenting with q4 and q3 for cost reasons.

00:02:48 - Liam Chen: we include q4, q5, and dynamic int8 profiles where feasible. note — the model quality delta can vary; Optimize will flag predicted degradation and recommend some A/B eval prompts.
00:03:00 - Maya Patel: showbench — I'm toggling a sample model (open-llama-7b variant) — see the right pane: kernel mapping, expected throughput on A100 vs A800 vs gpus, plus a compatibility score.
00:03:15 - Sophia Kim: that compatibility score — what's the weighting? latency vs quality vs memory?
00:03:20 - Aria Soto: it's configurable; default is 40% latency, 30% quality (eval suite), 20% cost, 10% infra-fit. you can change weights per project.
00:03:32 - Olivia Park: we care heavily about P95 latency. anything above 200ms P95 for short queries is a no-go for our main product path.

00:03:38 - Maya Patel: noted. we'll prioritize models with P95 under 200ms in the <=64 token bucket. also keep in mind prefix caching can reduce observed latency for repeated prompts — Optimize can recommend caching rules per route.
00:03:51 - Daniel Ruiz: can Optimize suggest batch sizes? Our throughput is small bursts; large batching hurts tail latency.

00:03:56 - Liam Chen: yes, Optimize has a policy generator — it takes your SLA (SLO) and traffic profile and outputs recommended batch sizes, max latency budget, and caching rules. you can export the policy to infra config.
00:04:08 - Ethan Brooks: how do fallbacks work? if the preferred low-latency model is saturated, what happens?

00:04:12 - Aria Soto: smart routing — policy can fallback to a slightly higher-latency but cheaper model, or route to Dedicated burst capacity. we also support region fallback if capacity is constrained.
00:04:22 - Olivia Park: data residency — we need everything to stay in EU for some customers. can the console filter by region-verified models?

00:04:28 - Maya Patel: yes — filter for region. plus Private deployment gives you a VPC-controlled plane. in that mode, traffic and logs can be kept inside your VPC, and we integrate with your KMS/HSM.
00:04:40 - Sophia Kim: audit logs — is there a structured export we can forward to our SIEM?

00:04:44 - Liam Chen: we export structured audit events and token-level usage traces; retention is configurable. for Private deployments we can ship logs directly to your log collector via secure forwarders.
00:04:55 - Maya Patel: demo time — switching to the bench runner. I'll queue a quick bench for two candidate models with Solaris sample prompts (Daniel's set).
00:05:05 - Daniel Ruiz: quick note — the sample prompts include a mix: short transactional queries, multi-turn banking dialogs, and a few doc-summary tasks.
00:05:12 - Aria Soto: cool. I'm going to show how we set up the bench: pick models, select hardware, set batch policy, and choose metrics: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, memory, and cost per 1k.
00:05:25 - 00:10:00 - [bench running - progress updates]

00:10:01 - Aria Soto: bench finished — quick highlights: Model A (7B q4 profile) gives ~120ms p95 on a8g for <=64 tokens, cost estimate $0.18 per 1k. Model B (13B fq) gives 210ms p95 on a8g but better quality on the summary tasks.
00:10:18 - Olivia Park: can we see the quality evals? like the rouge/qa scores used in the console?

00:10:22 - Liam Chen: yes, here's the eval tab — we run your prompts and compute a small set of metrics (exact match, rouge, a human-like score when available). for privacy, these evals can be run inside your Private deployment so data never leaves your env.
00:10:36 - Sophia Kim: is there a way to pin a model per route and have auto-fallback?

00:10:40 - Maya Patel: yep—route config supports pinned model, percent rollout, and automatic fallback chains with weightings. you can do canary 10% -> 25% -> 100% and set a rollback trigger on quality regression.
00:10:52 - Daniel Ruiz: regression alerting — does it compare to baseline prompts?
00:10:56 - Aria Soto: it ties to a prompt set you define. if the new rollout degrades below a threshold on those prompts, we trigger an alert and optionally auto-roll back.
00:11:06 - Ethan Brooks: mention of cost again — how accurate are the cost estimates?
00:11:10 - Liam Chen: estimates are within ~10-20% for typical traffic once you enable real telemetry. for initial planning it's coarse; that's why we wanted to run a bench with your actual prompts.
00:11:20 - Olivia Park: okay that's helpful. on security: we need SOC2 + some custom compliance Qs. you mentioned a security package?
00:11:26 - Maya Patel: yes, we'll send the security whitepaper and the SOC2 attestation. plus a short onboarding checklist for Private deployments (KMS integration, VPC peering, audit export).
00:11:34 - Sophia Kim: can Redwood's private control plane be air-gapped? we have one client that requires it.
00:11:38 - Liam Chen: there's an on-prem option with an air-gapped install — some features like hosted analytics require connectors, but we provide a bundle to run fully offline.
00:11:47 - Daniel Ruiz: question about KV cache — if we enable prefix caching, does it change memory profile and how much state do we store per key?

00:11:54 - Aria Soto: KV cache is configurable — typical footprint is small per key for short sequences, but it does increase VRAM usage proportionally. Optimize will recommend cache TTLs to balance hit rate vs memory.
00:12:05 - Olivia Park: any gotchas with tokenizer mismatch with open models? we've had issues with special tokens in the past.
00:12:11 - Liam Chen: tokenizer mismatches show up in our eval harness; the console flags tokenization drift and suggests canonical tokenizers or tokenizer wrappers.

00:12:20 - Maya Patel: we're about midway — let's surface a couple tradeoff scenarios. scenario A: strict latency SLO (<200ms) uses 7B q4 variant plus caching vs scenario B: better summary quality uses 13B fp16 but costs double. which do you prefer for your product?
00:12:35 - Olivia Park: for the main chat path we must hit latency SLO. for batch summaries we can accept higher latency. so maybe hybrid routing.
00:12:42 - Ethan Brooks: hybrid routing sounds right — pin 7B for chat, 13B for summaries, and configure automatic model routing based on route label.
00:12:48 - Sophia Kim: timeline-wise, what's realistic for a pilot? we want a POC in prod-like env in 4 weeks.

00:12:54 - Maya Patel: plausible — week 1 pick models and sign off on security checklist, week 2 bench runs and pilot infra setup (Dedicated or Private), week 3 integration and canaries, week 4 evaluate and decide on committed capacity.
00:13:05 - Daniel Ruiz: I'll need the bench runner config exported — docker file or job spec?
00:13:09 - Aria Soto: we export a bench job spec you can run in our hosted runner or re-run in Dedicated. we'll attach the exact kernel/quantization flags.
00:13:16 - 00:30:00 - [dive into compatibility matrix and exported CSVs, occasional side conversations, some audio degradation noted]
00:30:05 - Aria Soto: calling out an item — some models have known op regressions on certain old kernels; we annotate fallback kernels. that's why kernel mapping is in the matrix.
00:30:20 - Olivia Park: will you be able to match the bench results if we run in our private data center GPUs? our infra is older gen.
00:30:26 - Liam Chen: we'll do a bench on your target hardware as part of Dedicated onboarding. if kernels aren't optimized we'll either recompile or recommend a different model variant.
00:30:35 - Sophia Kim: what about throughput bursts? we have unpredictable traffic spikes during payroll runs.
00:30:40 - Maya Patel: we have burst policies and reserved headroom. you can configure autoscale thresholds and guaranteed burst capacity; billing only applies when burst capacity used.
00:30:50 - Daniel Ruiz: any example custom metric dashboards? I want to track cost per successful intent resolution, not just tokens.
00:30:56 - Aria Soto: you can plug in your eval metrics via API. the console supports custom metrics and alerting on those signals.
00:31:05 - Ethan Brooks: competitive question — we've looked at SageMaker endpoints; what's the primary benefit of Redwood for us?

00:31:10 - Maya Patel: quicker model selection with curated open model profiles, integrated Optimize recommendations, unified routing between hosted/dedicated/private, and production-grade fallbacks. also our eval/rollout tooling is more opinionated for LLM serving.
00:31:22 - Olivia Park: final block — procurement and contracts. do you have enterprise terms for Dedicated with a 12-month commit?
00:31:28 - Maya Patel: yes — we have reserved capacity contracts. I'll connect you with our sales ops and legal to share draft SOW and pricing tiers.
00:31:36 - Sophia Kim: one more compliance note — we need an encryption-at-rest spec for token caches and K/V stores.
00:31:41 - Liam Chen: our doc covers data at rest encryption, KMS integration patterns, and HSM options for Private installs. we'll send that in the package.
00:31:50 - 00:50:00 - [wrap-up, quick Q&A, some crosstalk, scheduling follow ups]

00:50:10 - Maya Patel: recap — action items: I'll share shortlist + cost spreadsheet; Liam will run bench with your prompts and export job spec; Sophia to confirm compliance list; Daniel to share prompt set. propose a follow-up pilot planning call next Wednesday at 10am PT.
00:50:30 - Olivia Park: that time works for me.
00:50:35 - Daniel Ruiz: works for me too.
00:50:40 - Sophia Kim: okay, thanks everyone.
00:50:45 - Maya Patel: thank you — we'll send notes and artifacts after the call. bye!
00:50:50 - [meeting ended]
